Subject: Medinex security discovery: network segmentation & evidence kickoff

Hi Mark / Elena,

Thanks again for the time this morning — really appreciated the clarity on your regulatory boundaries and the high-level architecture constraints for the private deployment. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the immediate asks and a practical plan for evidence and design artifacts so your security and procurement teams have what they need to move forward.

Summary of key constraints you mentioned:
- Primary region: US (east) for data residency.
- HIPAA applies to PHI in a subset of workflows; GDPR concerns for EU-sourced data to be addressed later if applicable.
- Preference for strong network isolation; potential air-gapped staging for model training artifacts.
- Procurement expects SOC 2 Type II status or concrete remediation roadmap and evidence.

Immediate deliverables we committed to:
1) Preliminary network segmentation diagram (VPCs, subnets, peering, NATs, bastions) — draft attached: redwood-vpc-reference-diagram.pdf.
2) Blank vendor security questionnaire pre-populated with answers where possible — attached: vendor-security-questionnaire-mdx-blank.xlsx.
3) SOC 2 status summary and roadmap showing controls in place and gaps with timelines — attached: soc2-internal-roadmap-summary.md.

Asks for Medinex to expedite:
- Please share your procurement questionnaire (if different from the attached) and any PoAM format you prefer.
- Confirm whether your compliance team needs evidence for logical separation of dev/test from prod (we can provide config extracts and interface lists).
- If you require an air-gapped option, confirm whether the staging environment needs physical air-gap or logical isolation with export controls.

Next steps / timeline:
- By EOD Wed (5/23): we’ll circulate a more detailed deployment sketch showing control points (bastion access, KMS boundaries, audit-log flows).
- Week of 5/29: Ben will run a short checkpoint with your security architect to review the questionnaire answers and request any supplemental logs.
- Week of 6/5: kickoff evidence handoff (S3 export, KMS policy screenshots, and test accounts) or DocuSign NDA if Medinex prefers a tighter exchange.

If helpful, I can also schedule a short 30-minute walkthrough of the attached diagram with your security and network folks.

Best,

Rafael Mendes

Mark — thanks for the intake doc. Ben and I reviewed and have pre-filled the questionnaire where we can; see the attached XLS (vendor-security-questionnaire-mdx-blank.xlsx).

Quick answers inline to your numbered asks:
1) KV cache boundary: our serving runtime keeps KV cache inside the model runtime instance; for private deployments we place the runtime in a private subnet with egress-controlled NAT and security groups. We can provide a hardened config that removes outbound internet egress from the runtime subnet and routes all outbound telemetry via an internal collector you control.
2) Audit logs: we write structured audit events to a customer-owned S3 bucket (or an on-prem file share) with JSONL format. Default retention via our platform is 90 days; for Private deployments we can configure retention to your policy and provide snapshots as compressed exports. We can also provide CloudTrail-style mapping for events.

Attachments included:
- vendor-security-questionnaire-mdx-blank.xlsx (pre-filled answers + comments)
- redwood-vpc-reference-diagram.pdf (updated with KV/cache callout)
- soc2-internal-roadmap-summary.md (notes on controls and expected Type II timeline)

Ben, Sean — can you be on standby next Tuesday (5/29) for the technical checkpoint with Medinex? I recommended 30 minutes focused on the KV/cache, egress controls, and evidence format.

Rafael
